extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent examination/prosecution staff
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of USPTO examination guidance and training materials covering statutory requirements (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112, 171), claim interpretation, interview practice, AIA/FITF issues, PTAB rules, and best practices for office actions and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility (35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject Matter Eligibility: guidance, examples, and training materials related to determining whether claimed subject matter is patent eligible under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance, Examples, and Training' (training modules and guidance referenced). Note: other training materials (e.g., written description materials) may include examples that now require further analysis for subject matter eligibility in view of recent law changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper anticipation rejections and 35 U.S.C. 102 practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on proper anticipation rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102, including reminders from recent case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part I - Proper Anticipation Rejections: Reminders from Recent Case Law (Spring 2018). Training materials and workshops on applying anticipation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness and 35 U.S.C. 103 practice (including KSR guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on making clear obviousness rejections, combined 102 & 103 workshops, and examination guidelines in view of KSR v. Teleflex for assessing obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part II - Clear Obviousness Rejections: Important Lessons from Outdry v. Geox (Summer 2018); Part III - Combined 102 & 103 Workshop (Summer/Fall 2018); 'Examination Guidelines and Training Materials in view of KSR Int’l Co. v. Teleflex Inc.' (through 2010 update).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining computer-implemented functional claim limitations (35 U.S.C. 112 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training focused on how to examine computer-implemented functional claim limitations for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Examining Computer-Implemented Functional Claim Limitations for Compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112' with Computer-Based Training (CBT) [posted 3/28/2019] and PowerPoint [posted 3/27/2019].

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — Written description (focus on electrical/mechanical and computer/software-related claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and training for assessing compliance with the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C. 112(a), with emphasis on electrical/mechanical and computer/software-related claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer Based Training (CBT) and PowerPoint materials: 'Examining Claims for Compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a): Overview and Part I - Written Description = Focus on Electrical/Mechanical and Computer/Software-related Claims' (CBT and PPT posted 08/17/2015). Includes Written Description Workshop and note about antibody decisions and compliance (PowerPoint posted 10/07/2015). Also includes archived 2008 Written Description Guidelines Training Materials with a notice that examples may now require further 101 analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(a) — Enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and guidance addressing enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a), with focus on electrical/mechanical and computer/software-related claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer Based Training (CBT) and PowerPoint: 'Examining Claims for Compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a): Part II - Enablement = Focus on Electrical/Mechanical and Computer/Software-related Claims' (CBT posted 10/15/2015; PPT posted 10/07/2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody decisions and written description compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials discussing how antibody-related claim examples are evaluated for compliance with the written description requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PowerPoint of the CBT on 'Antibody Decisions and Their Compliance with the Written Description Requirement' [posted 10/07/2015].

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(b) — Definiteness and functional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on ensuring claims are definite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b), including handling functional language and claim clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items include 'Enhancing Clarity By Ensuring That Claims are Definite Under 35 U.S.C. 112(b)' (PowerPoint [posted May 20, 2016]) and 'Functional Language Workshop: Claim Interpretation And Definiteness Under 35 U.S.C. 112(b)' (PPT [posted September 8, 2016]). Hands-on examples and worksheets provided (Ultrasonic Surgical Shears, Laundry Detergent, Computerized Color Editing) along with blank worksheets and answer keys.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112(f) — Means-plus-function limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for addressing means-plus-function claim limitations under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) in office actions and examination practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials: 'Addressing 35 U.S.C. § 112(F) or "Means-plus-Function" Limitations in an Office Action using New Form Paragraphs' Computer Based Training (CBT) [posted March 27, 2018]; Sample Office Action (PDF) and PDF of CBT [posted March 27, 2018]; Instructor-led training PPT and example background/claims and office actions for Chemical (Laundry Detergent), Electrical (Computerized Color Editing System), Mechanical (Ultrasonic Surgical Shears) (all PDFs posted March 27, 2018). Public comments invited to TrainingComments112f@uspto.gov. Also includes 'Supplementary Examination Guidelines for Determining Compliance With 35 U.S.C. 112' (signed January 21, 2011).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary examination guidelines for 35 U.S.C. 112 and related issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary guidelines and slide set for determining compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 and treatment of related issues in patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes '35 U.S.C. § 112 Supplementary Examination Guidelines' (PPT prepared from guidelines signed January 21, 2011) and training examples [posted May 20, 2011].

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional language worksheets and hands-on examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical exercises and worksheets to apply claim-definiteness and functional-language analysis in concrete hypothetical claim sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-On Examples and Functional Language Worksheets include: Example 1 (Ultrasonic Surgical Shears), Example 2 (Laundry Detergent), Example 3 (Computerized Color Editing), Blank worksheets, supporting reference info, and answer keys for each example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent examination (35 U.S.C. 171) — computer-generated interfaces and icons
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental guidance for examination of design patent applications related to computer-generated interfaces, icons, electronic images, and GUIs under 35 U.S.C. 171.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents: 'Supplemental Guidance for Examination of Design Patent Applications Related to Computer-Generated Interfaces and Icons' [PDF published March 13, 2026]; 'Supplemental Guidance for Examination of Design Patent Applications Related to Computer-Generated Electronic Images, Including Computer-Generated Icons and Graphical User Interfaces' [PDF published November 17, 2023]; Correction PDF [published January 29, 2024]; Correctly formatted Examples 2, 4, and 5 correction [PDF posted January 30, 2024].

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent examiner materials and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: General materials and resources for design patent examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Design patent examiner materials and resources' — collection of materials specific to design examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice (US Restriction Practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and guidance on U.S. restriction practice for patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'U.S. Restriction Practice' Computer Based Training (CBT) [Posted December 9, 2019] and a PowerPoint of the CBT [posted December 9, 2019].

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Training addressing the unity of invention standard and its application in examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Unity of Invention' Computer Based Training (CBT) [Posted December 9, 2019] and PowerPoint of the CBT [posted December 9, 2019].

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation — instructor-led interactive module
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive instructor-led training module on claim interpretation principles and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim Interpretation instructor-led interactive module [html] [posted May 14, 2019] and associated PowerPoint [posted May 14, 2019].

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining functional claim limitations — focus on computer/software-related claims
rubrics_metrics.description: CBT focused on examining functional claim limitations with emphasis on computer/software-related claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer Based Training 'Examining Functional Claim Limitations: Focus on Computer/Software-related Claims' [CBT posted June 30, 2015] and PowerPoint [posted June 30, 2015].

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) and plain meaning of claim terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Training on applying the broadest reasonable interpretation standard and determining the plain meaning of claim terms during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer Based Training (CBT) 'Broadest Reasonable Interpretation (BRI) and the Plain Meaning of Claim Terms' [CBT posted March 3, 2015] and PowerPoint [posted March 3, 2015].

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview practice and best practices for examiner-interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and training on conducting interviews with applicants/attorneys, including best practices and summaries of interview training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials include 'Interview Practice Training' (2015) and training summary; 'Effective Interview Practice' (2012); 'Interview Best Practices' (2011); 'Interview Practice Training Summary' (2009); and 'Awareness Workshop' as part of interview practice resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices in examination (including compact prosecution)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level best practices for examination and prosecution, including techniques for compact prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items include 'Best Practices in Examination', 'Best Practices in Compact Prosecution (2009)', and other overview materials to improve efficiency and prosecution quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving clarity and reasoning in office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Training aimed at improving the clarity and legal/technical reasoning used in office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'Improving Clarity and Reasoning in Office Actions Training' — likely includes modules, examples, and writing guidance for office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to legal arguments and legal analysis writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Training on understanding case law, evaluating and analyzing legal arguments, and writing persuasive replies to attorney arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Part I: Understanding Case Law and the Federal Court System' (Computer Based Training [posted January 3, 2017]); 'Part II: How to Evaluate and Analyze Legal Arguments Based on Case Law' [posted September 11, 2017]; 'Part II Legal Analysis Writing Workshop Slides - with Talking Points' (April 2017); 'Part II Legal Analysis Writing Worksheet - Blank Worksheet' and 'Answer Key' (April 2017); and 'Part III: Writing a Persuasive Reply to Attorney Arguments' (January 2019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance describing reasons and criteria for allowing patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed item 'Reasons for Allowance (2016)' — training material addressing when and why claims should be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112 — sample office actions and form paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates, sample office actions, and new form paragraphs for addressing 35 U.S.C. 112 and related issues in office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Sample Office Action (for use with the CBT)' [PDF posted March 27, 2018] in connection with 35 U.S.C. 112(f) training; guidance on using new form paragraphs to address means-plus-function limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: America Invents Act (AIA) — First Inventor To File (FITF) training and framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and reference materials implementing the AIA First-Inventor-to-File framework for examination practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials include 'First-Inventor-to-File Training Plan for USPTO Examiners' [PDF]; 'First-Inventor-to-File Statutory Framework Chart' [PDF]; Overview CBT (March 2013) with video and slides [PDF]; Overview Follow-On video (March 2013); FITF Definitions (June 2013) video and slides and handout; Comprehensive Examiner Training Slides (Summer 2013) video and slides; AIA FITF Indicator Training (Fall 2013); FITF Evidentiary Declarations (Winter 2014) video and slides; and 'Interference Searches in AIA (FITF) Applications' (2015) [PDF].

rubrics_metrics.name: non-FITF AIA regulations training
rubrics_metrics.description: Training on AIA regulations that do not relate to the FITF framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as 'non-FITF Regulations Training (Summer 2013) [PDF]'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) / Rules of Practice in ex parte appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on rules and practice before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (formerly BPAI) for ex parte appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes 'Rules of Practice Before the BPAI in Ex Parte Appeals (2012)' and contact direction to the Office of Patent Legal Administration for questions regarding the content of the web page.
